brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A silver-downed green tea from around Taibai Peak, the summit of the Tongbai Mountains on Henan's southern edge.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It was named a Henan famous tea in 1986 and rated a quality tea by the national agriculture ministry in 1989. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Picked, spread, fixed, rolled, shaped into strands, worked to bring out the down, then dried.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Bold, firm strands fully covered in silver down, a moist green.
taste_profile: Tender aroma with a mellow, brisk taste.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
